environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; one client socket per composition, strict-token peer with a monotonic SEQ counter echoed into the body, hex-exact client capture

findings.description: `GET /api%2fexec%20?cmd=id&mode=sub%20n=60` plus two pipelined followers. Client bytes: `HTTP/1.1 100 Error` + `Content-Length: 60`, then the real `200` head as body, `SEQ:1 TOK:` truncated at exactly 60 bytes, then the followers' two responses. Each response carries the previous request's SEQ, so an innocent pipeliner reads executed bytes as the body of a response it did ask for, and its own last response is orphaned. Boundary: an interim CL below the body leaves `HTTP/1HTTP/1.1 200 OK` in the window and the client parser breaks; an interim CL above everything plus a follower is a flat 502, so the usable window is interim-CL between the real body and the following head.
findings.title: An interim 100 carrying a Content-Length becomes a terminal head; the real head is absorbed as its body and every later answer on the socket shifts one request

limitations: Intra-connection only; no cross-client leak was found
Needs an attacker-influenced upstream and a pipelining client
All RCE is RCE on the upstream host
